tips.comment: This horse caught the eye on hurling debut, and they have stepped Western Clouds up in trip today. That looks like the right thing to do. I fancy this horse will be tough to beat today.

Made hurdles debut at Clonmel on the 6th of June and was well supported in the market into a 5/1 shot in an 18-runner maiden hurdle. Was tenderly handled after making some jumping errors at crucial times and eventually came home a well-beaten 5th. Encouraging enough on debut but will have learned plenty, and the 4/1 on offer today could look very generous after the race.

Palm Beach is an 8-year-old gelding making a stable debut for Ben Pauling and ridden by Ben Jones. He has won two non-handicap hurdles off official marks of 119-124 and also won over 12f on the flat, so is clearly well handicapped. Ben has ridden 77 of Ben Pauling's winners since 2012, so they make a very good team. Palm Beach starts life with Pauling on a very appealing mark of just 77, as Ben Pauling's record with stable switchers is second to none: 20/121 wins and 41/121 places since 2012. Ben Jones has ridden three stable debutants for Ben Pauling since 2024, and 2 of the 3 won: Groovy Blue at 9-1 and Rocks Up Late at 11-2, and finished 8/11 on Squire Danagher. Palm Beach is my short-priced banker of the day.

Raby Mere is a sound choice in a bad race. Rushed out quick after winning on debut this season was a mistake, but has won both of the other runs, which in this field counts for a lot. Trainer and jockey combo are one of the best, and this to me looks very winnable.

Top Flight Century is a lightly raced 4-year-old gelding with just four starts. He posted a career-high RPR of 78 on handicap debut at Perth when beaten just 6 lengths under notable jockey booking Brian Hughes, 25+1 into 16-1. So he has his supporters. He's been dropped a 1lb despite the good effort, and this ex-Sir Mark Prescott horse is stepped up in trip off 76 with Joshua Thompson's 7lb claim. This should suit, being related to two smart middle-distance performers who posted career-high RPRs of 98-122. Top Flight Century looks like a knocking each-way possible if the gamble on Palm Beach is foiled. Put both in a RFC.
Would have been placed from this mark last time around here over shorter. This represents a drop in grade, so should be in the money at least.

The model I run suggests Malangen can win this one and cause an upset. This result has been driven by Malangen having the second highest RPR of the 12-horse race but has an official ranking that leaves him looking well treated off this mark. Has shown glimpses of coming back into form with figures of 60-543 and getting closer to getting over the line first. Last out 11 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern. Needs to find a bit more. Jockey relieves 3 lbs, which helps around this 2m 4f trip and is a prior course and distance winner, so knows how to get it done around this track. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Shantou Lucky has not been great since winning last September and taking on weight. While still not great this year, I am putting my hopes in the fact that he has dropped to an 83 and is now second up after wind surgery, which is when I would expect to see more improvement. EW 4P.

Blow A Fortune returns from a layoff after PU in December. The unexposed five-year-old is up against some experienced horses here, yet showed on the penultimate run she has ability. She stayed on late over 2m good at Ayr for 4th, less than a length behind the 2nd who is now rated 98. With the step up in trip likely to bring more from her and the assistance of Brian Hughes, there is fair EW value at 16/1 currently on offer.

Reverts to hurdling after a spell chasing and pointing. He has dropped to a career-low mark and while recent efforts are nothing to write home about, it was just over twelve months ago that he was finishing second over two miles at today's venue, and he's thirteen pounds lower today. He has won over further than today's trip so has no stamina issues, and conditions should suit. Given recent form, or lack of it, he is a speculative bet at best, but no world beaters in opposition, and his favorable racing weight is further reduced by his useful jockey's five-pound claim.

Has won over course and distance four times. Last race, though only third, was a poor performance only enhanced by the fact she kept on till the finish. That was three weeks ago, and today she faces a horse with three straight wins. However, I would be surprised if she didn't finish in the top three.

Handicapper has given him a chance here. Dropping him 3lbs for his last run. Which in truth wasn't a bad effort. 
He ran a decent enough race lto. Bumping into the Irish challenger Impero. Beaten 10L by the winner admittedly. He did pull 11L clear of the 3rd horse however. 
He boasts a win and 2 places from 5 runs at this track. With the win coming off a 2lbs lower mark than this. He's got a little bit of work to do to reverse form with Just Dottie based on his penultimate run. Having finished 5L behind that horse. He's 5lbs better off with that horse this time. 
The yard are in fine fettle at the moment. The ground is in his favour. He should go well on these terms.

Winds Of Winter won at Cartmel on good to soft and then followed up at Hexham once more on good to soft, which she will be meeting for the third time, as it rained all day yesterday and more than likely been the same at Perth. Johnathan Bewley has the ride for a family relative, George Bewley. She won by eleven lengths at Hexham by sitting off the pace and staying on really well, which she can bring to the third with being in good form.

Spit Spot is one of the younger and possibly more progressive horses in this race, could show some improvement today, unexposed at handicap level. Ran well over a slightly longer distance last time out, faded late on so this small drop in trip could be much more suitable.

Caldwell is having his first run back from a rest so he may just need the run but, this good , in-form trainer usually has them in good shape first time back from a rest. This horse does have good form in the book at this level , can be running well from this current rating.
This looks like a good opportunity for this Rutherford horse to add to recent wins, one of those being over C&D. It still looks to be well handicapped.

Iain Jardine can take this with his ex-Irish stable debutante Shuil Na Tra, who last won at Sligo in August last year while still trained by Norman Lee. There has been a fair amount of money for him here from an early price of 10/1 down to his current price of about 4/1.

Maillot Blanc won here last time by a short distance of a neck from Happygolucky Index. When winning by this distance with staying on, the horse may have more in the locker that can see delivering another big run with five pounds more.
No Rematch has improved this year since having wind surgery and got back handicapping in May to a C4 second. He seems on a decent mark for this drop back to C5.

The model I run suggests Burgundy Man can win this one. This result has been driven by Burgundy Man having a comparably high RPR to the other runners in this 10-horse field but an official ranking that leaves him looking relatively well treated off. Goes out carrying just shy of 1 stone less than the current market favorite and top weight over this 2m 7f trip. Form looks to be improving with a good second when last time out 24 days ago and looks to go one better here. Model has issued a 'very low' stakes indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
This gelding looks good value to me. The yard is going well, and the horse has won his last 4 completed starts. A three-pound rise for his Kelso win shouldn't stop him.

DALILEO brings the all-important course and distance winning form. He would have likely been in need of his comeback run latest to help set him straight and from those in the second half of the market he can be given a realistic chance of framing up.

Wheresmymoneygone showed little in 4 starts under rules, but he won a maiden point in good style in April and has since joined Ben Pauling. He looks to have a good chance here off a lowly starting handicap mark on chase debut.

Olly Murphy and Sean Bowen, champion jockeys, hardly leave Perth without a winner or two or more. Summerleaze can produce a big run over fences for the first time, with Sean having the mount on the correct leg to make this run here a positive one.

Euchan Falls won consecutive hurdle races early in 2023, and those remain his only wins after several attempts, including thirteen in chases in which he has been 2nd five times, including here at Perth. Just in the handicap here off his lowest mark of 76 on ten stone two pounds, and could go close again in this competitive handicap in which several like to make the pace.

The model I run suggests Ballydangan can win this one. This result has been driven by Ballydangan having a comparably high RPR to the other runners in this 12-horse race, but an official ranking that leaves him looking fairly well treated off this mark. Goes out carrying over a stone less than current market favorite Bumpy Evans and even more weight lighter than the top weight. Has shown signs of form when coming first 19 days ago and looks to get over the line first again here. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

This horse is one of the older horses in this race so he could be vulnerable to the younger and slightly more progressive rivals but, he's still running to a decent level. Better effort last time out which suggests he's possibly on the way back into some better form now so from what looks like a fair rating, he's one to consider.

Carnet de Stage is difficult to win with, but has run well the last two times, including once over this trip in May. Last time out was encouraging to begin with before the confidence was knocked before a dismount. But if you are prepared to forgive that, we've got one that could outrun this price.

The model I run suggests Nathan Wells can cause an upset in this one. This result has been driven by Nathan Wells having a comparably high RPR to the other 7 runners but has an official ranking that is the lowest. This subsequently means Nathan Wells goes out carrying the lowest amount of weight around this 2m 4f round trip. Last out 19 days ago, so race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Trained by Robert Llewelyn, who rarely sends runners up to this course. Has two career wins, both in this class of race. Has won off a higher handicap mark. Finished second last time out at Uttoxeter, beaten a head over two and a half miles. This looks a weaker standard and can go one better today.

El Muchacho, with Sean Bowen in the plate for Olly Murphy. He was pulled up at Newton Abbot where he was at the back with Harry Cobden and stayed until Harry called it a day. Possibly something amiss and never gave true running. This afternoon, the Scottish air may be to his liking with Sean Bowen making a play from off the pace with a big run appearing.

Small each-way tip for this horse who runs for a trainer who's horses often run well at this course. This horse looked to find the longer distance too much of a stretch last time out, may well do better today now dropping back down a fair way in distance. This horse does have good form in the book at this cover over a similar distance to this.
Looks like a significant jockey booking to me with Ryan Moore riding this one on debut. The bookies obviously think this as well. The trainer does well at this course and could add to its win tally.

Standard set by Conjecture, but she was outpaced before staying on over a mile at Beverley. Winner ran a better final furlong despite FS 102.9%. Best Run-Out speed (34.31 mph) suggests she wants further. Yard 0.85 A/E where 2YO placed on debut. William Haggas can be backed blind at Yarmouth to a profit (31% SR where SP 1-3), but with FTO 2YOs, records 1.12 A/E, 28.9% SR where SP Pos 1-3, +£4.12 LSP to £1 Stake.

Conjecture had a duff start on debut last month and lost it in the final furlong. She fell to the back of the pack but fought back to grab second in the final strides and could be bang in there now second up, if getting a better start.

Shining Guest is a 2yo filly trained by George Margarson and ridden by Kieran O'Neill. She makes her 2yo debut. She is by Starman, a 75,000gns yearling out of a pretty ordinary dam, Under Offer (IRE), and a half-sister and fourth foal to three individual winners. Amazing Athena, trained by Jimmy Murtagh, won on her second start as a 2yo. Bonbon, trained by J P O'Brien, won on her third start as a 2yo, and Basil Martini, also trained by J P O'Brien, won a 2yo Group 3 at the Curragh, posting a career-high RPR of 98. So, Shining Guest has a pretty precocious pedigree line. It's a big ask on debut as the trainer is not renowned for his 2yo winners, but at the price in a small field, it could turn into a tactical affair. The sire Starman is also making waves with 14/76 wins, 29/76 placed, and has had 6 debut winners. His progeny have picked up 2 Group races, nearly won the Group 2 Queen Mary Stakes at Royal Ascot at 100-1, and won with Lady Iman at Naas and Venetian Sun at Royal Ascot. It's possible!
This is the trainer's only runner today after a withdrawal in the 1st race. That horse was likely his better chance, but I will try this one to go well under his claimer.
Just three starters here. Starshiba showed good performance in his last race in Nottingham one week ago. He was very close to winning. I think he can do it today. The jockey is still Jack Dace.

Yippee! I may bore a hole in my head. A 3-runner hand and heels apprentice handicap, and you pick a horse who previously found a mile a stretch. Well, at least it will place. Seriously, taking the weight into consideration, it has a good chance assuming all is as it should be.

Can perform much better than the last time out effort when only 11 of 11 at Doncaster. But the good news is that she won here back in April of this year, which is off the same mark now when you factor in the 3lb claimer.
The form of his debut third at Nottingham has worked out well and that makes him the one to beat in this field.

Was a staying on 4th on debut in a Class 2 event over 6f at Yarmouth in May when looking in need of the experience. That was in a field of newcomers and has already produced a couple of winners. Improved on that last time at Newbury when 3rd without coming under too much pressure and can improve again here and go close.

Charlie Appleby's record with 2YO debutantes at Yarmouth: 35.5% SR where SP Pos 1-3, +£6.71 to £1 Stakes. Kodi Bear Colt, Sire 26% SR with 2YOs where SP Pos 1-3, LSP +£9.48 to £1 Stakes, 1.03 A/E. Cost 500k as a yearling. First 2YO runner for Godolphin by Kodi Bear. Dam winner over 7f as a 2YO. Dougie Costello on 2YOs for Godolphin, +£17.83 LSP to £1 Stake, 37.5% SR, 1.48 A/E. Peel Park ranked 6th for final furlong when 3rd at Newbury, High Approval 5th at Nottingham and 10th for Top Speed Metric. Not an impossible standard set.

Reception is a 2yo colt trained by Charlie Fellowes. He has the benefit of two runs under his belt in this class 4 maiden. He is out of a dam called Tamara Love (IRE), who was pretty ordinary, but Reception is a half-brother to the useful Room Service, RPR 115. Room Service, trained by Kevin Ryan, is 4/12 wins and won a Listed race at Doncaster as a 2yo and finished 2/8 in a Group 3 last June behind the vastly improved Quinault, now rated 112 and a winner of 10 races. He is also related to four-time winner Royal Advice, RPR, both performing best over today's 6f. Reception was beaten 2l last time out at Chester over 7f despite racing wide under Billy Loughnane, so he did well in the circumstances and was heavily backed 100-30 into 2-1. With experience on his side, he can make his presence felt in this company for Charlie Fellowes under Stevie Donahue, for a trainer who has had 45 2yo winners with 22 winners if reappearance is within the last 25 days. He is dropped back down to 6f as he didn't quite see out the trip at Chester over 7f. Interesting contender!
Museum Piece is a 2-year-old who has been most successful over 5f. His most recent 5f race was his only win at Wolverhampton, where he beat Flowerhead, who went on to finish 2nd at Ascot.

The trainer places her horses selectively, and her last runner was a winner. She is using a promising 5lb claiming apprentice here who has been picking up rides for the Gosden stable, and he looks good value for his claim. The first-time cheekpieces could be the key here, which are added to the tongue tie. The first time the tongue tie was used resulted in the horse's best run when 3rd of 9 under a very similar trip and ground as she gets here. Crucially, the horses around her that day would suggest she could have plenty in hand off this mark of 54 (she could be a high 60s horse on that evidence).

King Of War last won back in 2023, but he was runner-up 3 times last year. Having his first start of the year and giving weight away to all his rivals might look like a tough task, but he is starting this season from an all-time low handicap mark. He has gone well fresh in the past. Track conditions look ideal, so a big run is expected.

Spanish Mane only missed out by a neck off a 58 at 7f when last here in April. While the latest run was only to fourth, that was at 1 mile. I think the return here at 7f off a 56 today with Laura back in the saddle, who was on top for that last win, could be in with an EW 5P chance.

Just five career runs for the 3yo and room for improvement. He was a decent 3rd on his handicap debut during May. Only 6th of 12 last time out over 12f, but he still held every chance a furlong out despite being keen in the race. The winner that day is now rated 86 and he shouldn’t fear these 62-68 rated runners over this shorter trip.

Glitter Code looks like a classic improver in a 3YO handicap, consistently placing without breaking through??'until now. Dropping weight via a 7lb claimer and drawn well, she faces exposed rivals. If she maintains form, she could spring a surprise at juicy odds.

At 6 years old she is the oldest horse in the race against the rest of the field who are all 3 year olds. She is 4 times a winner at this track, three times over course and distance and that winning experience could stand her in good stead here.

Backing Saliko, the lightly raced 3-year-old bay filly by Kameko, now trained by Jack Jones, in tomorrow’s Mark Sumner Handicap over 1m 2f 23y at Yarmouth. She arrives in good form after consistent maidens??'finishing third at Beverley (28 May) and second at Brighton (8 May)??'both over around 7 furlongs on good ground, showing she's sharp and has potential to step up successfully in trip .
This rise to middle distances suits her pedigree and recent stamina signs, and though stepping into handicap company, her current mark of 68 looks fair given her promise.

This Kodi Bear gelding highlighted his experience effortlessly, clinching victory in a 6-runner novice at Ripon 14 days ago, running the rail and establishing a clear lead. I expect he will remain competitive as he transitions to nurseries.
Blue To Blue had a cracking debut when winning a C3 but had all sorts of problems last time out. He seems on a decent mark for this handicap debut, with the step up to 6f likely to suit.

Mister Moet has been improving since a hard fall in its debut. It broke its maiden in the last start (3rd race) on Monday in a higher category. Today it is its handicap debut, and greater improvement is expected.

Born Slippy is a 2yo colt trained by Richard Spencer. He makes his nursery debut after three promising runs. On his penultimate start, he was hotly beaten by 2 lengths, finishing 2/8 and keeping on well in the closing stages over 5f at Chepstow. So today's step up to 6f could see him in a better place. He is a half-brother to four winners and out of a dam called Rose Blossom, who was very talented. She had 5 wins out of 21 starts with an RPR of 109 and was a three-time winner over today's 6f. She won a listed race at Doncaster and a Group 3 at York over 6f and placed a further four times in Listed races and placed in another Group 3. She thrived around this time of year, winning three races in July (2) and August. Born Slippy has three runs under his belt now and can capitalize on any subpar performance from today's favorite, Front Line Fury, who looks like the one to beat.

Just five career runs for the 4yo filly and still unexposed. Two runs this year, both in handicap company, and she hasn’t been beaten far in both races. Plenty of winners have come out of those two races, she runs off the same mark again and William Buick taking over in the saddle is a big positive.
The yard is going very well at the moment, and this horse is only two pounds higher than her last win. The slight drop in trip and the sharp track should suit.

Horse number 2, who is currently favourite can be running well but, looking at the previous form of that horse suggests this trip may be on the short side for that one. Princess Niyla will be needing improvement now moving back up in distance but, she has kept on well over a shorter distance in recent races so that offers some hope of a good run today and this is a drop in Class for this horse, may do a bit better in this easier Class. Very small each-way tip

The last 20 races True Promise has competed in have been Class 4 or Class 3. This is his first try in Class 5 company. If the first-time blinkers help him concentrate on today's job in hand, there is every reason to believe this race will be a lot easier than the 20-runner, £25k race at York last time. Yet to win on turf, but is effective at 5/6 furlongs.
Glory Fighter is very versatile as far as trip and ground go. So the quicker going here won't hinder chances of making it 2 wins in 3 runs after a win at Nottingham and a third at Catterick.
Great form figures 231122. Two firsts from May on AW. He's a course and distance winner, so should firmly be amongst the action at the post.

The 5yo mare has good career stats over this 5f C/D. Back from a 4-month break two weeks ago, maybe going a little too quick when making the running and outpaced late on, but she saw the race out. She faced rivals rated 79-85 that day, now up against 57-75 rated runners. With the jockey’s claim in this apprentice riders’ handicap, she’s effectively 7lb better off now.

Declan Carroll's horse, nothing went right for this one last time out at Thirsk. It went off as the favorite but stumbled leaving the stalls and then did not get the best of runs. Might bounce back with a tongue strap fitted and breaking on terms.

Soul Seeker is an 8-year-old gelding trained by Philip Kirby and has done nothing in three starts since leaving David O'Meara, who won 9 out of 54 races on turf for the previous trainer. He is a 9-time winner over 5f and a CD winner and loves to hear his feet rattle, winning 9 times on good or good to firm ground. His last win came off today's mark of 68 by 2.75 lengths under Jason Watson (no claim) and runs today off a lowly 61 with an apprentice taking off 7lb. He also comes to hand this time of year, winning 7 out of 9 of his races in July/August/September, with 3 in July. There are a couple of negatives in Donagh Murphy, is 0-12 wins, and Philip Kirby hasn't had a flat winner in any of his last 66 runners on the flat and 128 days since last, but given conditions are optimal, there remains some hope in this small field (4 out of 9 wins in fields of 7 runners or less). A chancex is taken at 16-1 with 3 places available with some bookmakers.

This one is shaping like a win is on the cards. It has a lot more to offer and was well suited being stepped up in trip. Ground conditions should be spot on. A good ride from the jockey should have us on the winning side.

Three runs this year for the 3yo, getting his act together two weeks ago over this 7f trip. Smoothly hitting the front a furlong out and was an easy 2L winner in the end. He can take another step forward and a 4lb higher mark might not stop him from following up.
The Andrew Balding yard is in fine form at the present time, and Captain Harry could be another that can go close to giving the yard another winner after a decent run last time at Kempton.

Coeur Jaune, I expect, should perform well today, liking the good/firm course and the distance. Has yet to win but does show potential and is improving. Out of Mehmas, who shows a high strike rate with 3-year-olds, and the trainer and jockey are in decent form. E/W potential.

Really unlucky LTO after bumping into some traffic when travelling very well into the race. Trainer is in form at the moment and I think 6/1 are good odds considering they've only left a 9-day gap between runs. Playing EW.

Anthropologist looks worth taking on a 2/1 having gone up in the weights for winning a weak race at Ayr. Captain Harry is one of two Andrew Balding brings up to the meeting from Kingsclere and is interesting. But Groundsman catches the eye. He looks to be coming into some form and ran well enough when unfancied in a 7f Class 4 at Thirsk. The race has a solid look to it and the first three home have all upheld the form subsequently.
Yet to win from 7 starts but did finish a good 3rd at Kempton on penultimate start. Each way chance again if finding that form today.
Improved on a promising debut 5th place here to finish 2nd at Sandown last month. That form is probably better than anything in this race and with further improvement likely, could go 1 better.
Makes his debut today under William Buick for Charlie Appleby who won this race last year. Big player in this race.

PROTECTION ACT is a well-bred, unraced two-year-old colt by Starspangledbanner. He is a half-brother to City Tour, a winner at 7f and 1m 3f. The course distance and going should suit him. He should run well on his racecourse debut and could well be able to win this race.
Made an encouraging debut at Newbury in a 6.5f minor event, finishing 4th without coming under too much pressure when making late headway. Capable of better and should feature.

Crown Of Light is a 2-year-old colt trained by William Knight. He landed two 2-year-old debutant winners at 14-1 (both attracted minor support) with Time Test, owned by today's owner Abdulla Al Mansoori, at Lingfield and Amakhala Warrior here at Haydock on 21/07/2024. Owner Abdulla Al Mansoori has amassed 198 winners here in the UK and various countries abroad and has landed some 30 big race wins. Crown Of Light is out of an unraced dam related to 6/6 individual winners, notably Magny Cours, 8/20 wins owned by Godolphin trained by A Fabre, won a Group 3 and two Listed races in France, RPR 118, a half-brother to four individual winners, all owned by Abdulla Al Mansoori and all trained by Ismail Mohammed, notably Good Effort, a 9-time winner and a 3-time Listed winner at Lingfield, RPR 114.
Perfect Ruler boasts elite pedigree, trained by course specialist Haggas, and ridden by top jockey Tudhope; strong breeding mix of speed and stamina suggests she’s primed for a winning debut.

Lady Gormire is a 2-year-old filly trained by Kevin Ryan (339 yo winners since 2012 80 of which won on their debut. She is sired by the useful Lope De Vega and is owned by Sheikh Mohammed Obaid Al Maktoum, who is a 59-time winner from 234 2-year-old runners on turf in the last five years. His horses are in fine fettle, winning with 5 of his last 7 runners. Lady Gormire is a full sister to Involvement and is 2/9 wins trained by Simon & Ed Crisford and recorded a RPR of 108. Out of a dam, Lady Of Dubai, who won a listed race at Goodwood and placed in a listed race at Newmarket, and got beat 2.5 lengths in the Investec Oaks. She may need further in time, but trainer Kevin Ryan won this race in 2022/2023, so she may be primed and ready on debut. However, two concerns are the application of a hood and the booking of Shane Gray, who is 0-14 at Haydock but has ridden 32 winners since 2012.

Really well bred lots of speed in the family. Owners known for having classy horses especially for the shorter distances.
Ed Bethell has 27% strike rate when teaming up with Connor Beasley.
Owners have 21% strike rate at Haydock with their horses.

Wren Runner is in stall number 9. This 2yo chestnut filly by Kameko showed signs when finishing seventh, beaten 6 and a half lengths on debut in a Goodwood maiden over 6, racing freely and doing too much early. Trainer Andrew Balding's juveniles often improve from their first run, and the yard is going well. The step up in trip may help if she settles better, and although the draw is not ideal, she can improve. Each-way shout.

Small each-way tip for Maw Can who is making her debut in what is a decent race. Newcomers from this trainer often run well first time out, she's drawn well. Has some good form in her pedigree, mainly over further trips but for now, 6f is an ideal starting point. Very small each-way tip.
Dysart Enos' debut on the flat/AW hasn't been beaten in 3 bumpers, including at Aintree. Never been short of pace, so should be one to consider here.
Showed little on debut, but expect better today. The stable has now started to come good, especially with its all-weather runners, and could get off the mark here.

Glint Of Light is in stall number 6. This 3-year-old filly by Cracksman shaped well on both starts to date, especially when finishing second, beaten 5 lengths in a 12 maiden at Lingfield last time out where she was well backed and kept on well behind the winner. She has shown me ability on debut too, and the step up in trip is a good move. Trained by Hughie Morrison and ridden again by Rob Hornby, with 2 career starts so far, she has yet to win but has a 50% place rate here. This also looks a slightly easier task, and if she progresses again, she should be involved.

Farasi Lane has not won since winning here in April last year off an 89. But this year was second in March off an 87 in a C2 and has continued to drop down the weights. Today is on an 82 with a handy 7 lbs claimer on top in C4.

Pulled really hard last time out and still managed to finish strongly over 7f on soft ground. An extra furlong on the all-weather (already proven to go well) will help, and stall 5 allows him to be handy on the tight right-hander that is Kempton.
Al Ameen drifted a little to 6/1, which is a good each way. Won last time here and could do the same again. 0.5 points each way.
Chalk Mountain can definitely place as has run well in the past in Kempton and with the added bonus ability to excel from any gate will definitely be among the top 3

Metaverse won a C3 here back in April off an 84 but has been pants for the last two runs on turf. However, that has dropped him back to an 86 and he could be involved again now back here on the AW. EW

Gelded son of Invincible Army & Roger Sez ( Dam's sire Red Clubs ) who was last seen at this venue 79 days ago racing at the 7 furlong trip where finishing 5th/10 arrives here in top nick and in very good heart now dropping back down in trip to the 6 furlong trip here at Kempton that being a good move by his connections as a race of this nature here at the polytrack of Kempton can really suit R M Beckett's inmate well now returned to a sprinting distance currently operating on a mark of 68 this individual should have a much bigger performance in the locker just waiting to unleashed and he should be capable of much better than a mark of 68 so from this point on in my point of view he should leave this mark well behind jockey Hector Crouch takes the ride and can give Invincible Melody the perfect ride here at Kempton merits serious consideration here
Azuinthejungle, a 3-year-old chestnut gelding, won last time out in a 0-60 apprentice handicap. Runs again off only 58 and should run his race.

Improvements are required to have any chance tomorrow, and the raised mark makes life harder. This is a course debut, so going into the unknown, but it's early days. I think he might be better suited to AW.
Has a 5lb claimer for tomorrow and has been in good form. But did struggle LTO when only 7 of 8 at Wolverhampton last October. But mark remains unchanged given his ability and can bounce back.
Siempre Arturo should easily win this today Gone down in price and a well-backed favorite today. 0.5 points watch way for me

Runner-up over half a furlong further at Chester at the end of May when last seen, but won over course and distance in the race subsequent to that. Just 4 pounds higher than that course and distance win, and the runner-up has won since too, to boost the form.

Won a 0-95 over course and distance last September off 86. Comes here off 89, down in grade. Can put a line through reappearance run last time, having no luck in running. Worth an e/w bet in this grade.

I thought this one looked a touch overpriced, having been far from disgraced on seasonal return. That race knits a few of this together, and whilst he’s got some work to do to turn around the form, all bar one horse was coming into that with at least a run under their belt. This horse wasn’t able to get as forward perhaps as he’d like, and in stall 1 here, his chance may be over if he doesn’t break well. A lack of an out-and-out front runner in the race should make that easier for him, you’d hope. A 2lb drop for that reappearance looks a fair gift to me if he can get out and dominate the pace, which is clearly no given in a big field.

Backing Incensed, the 4-year-old Ulysses filly now trained by Amanda Perrett, in tomorrow’s 12f Class 3 Kempton Handicap (6:58 GMT). She returns off a solid reappearance outing at Sandown on June 13, where she finished 5th of 8 over 1m 1f??'the first run since her transfer from Andrew Balding and a near 9-month break, marking her as race-sharp and building .
Her profile shines more brightly in the all-weather sphere: she’s already notched an AW win in September 2024 at Kempton over this same 1m 3f 219y trip, scoring by an impressive 4 lengths . That effort showcases her ability to handle the Kempton surface and suggests she’s well-suited returning to this course and trip.
Stepping back into Class 3 company, she looks well-treated on a mark of 83, especially now on her favoured AW surface, with fitness and confidence under the belt. Expect her to settle in midfield before delivering a telling move in the final furlong. With trainer Amanda Perrett finding form and the race shaping up to suit a proven AW performer, she offers solid each-way value in a competitive field.

Flash Bardot has previously run well fresh. Ready winner of a Class 3 handicap over 1m4f on seasonal debut last year from OR85. Rose Dawes claims 5lbs off of the 87 rating this year. Trainer Jack Channon (SR 42%) in strong form currently and jockey rode a winner from last two rides. The 5yo mare still looks well handicapped. Continued to progress last season. This may be a slightly delayed return and it's a hot race but got to be respected. Good all weather form.

Way of Life is interesting, receiving weight all around over a course and distance that is proven to suit. Form lines are encouraging too, so at these odds, I think this horse represents good each-way value, ridden by a jockey that has gotten results with him before.
This could be a quick-fire double for the jockey/trainer combo. It ran well in all three of its outings so far, and off this reasonable rating on handicap debut, it is surely better than this.

Thrice raced daughter of Kodiac & Woodland Maiden ( Dam's sire Mastercraftsman ) who was last seen at Bath 19 days ago where finishing a respectable 3rd/10 makes her handicap debut here off a very attractive mark of 70 and she can progress very well now heading down the handicap route and this class 5 nursery handicap is the perfect starting point for this individual steps up in trip here racing at the 7 furlong trip for the first time that most certainly being a good move by her connections as this new trip can bring out further improvement and she is open to plenty of progress and has shaped with promise that this trip will be spot on ideal jockey Hector Crouch takes the ride on Ollie Sangster's inmate and can give Whisperwood a promising ride here at Kempton and jockey Hector Crouch is worth following at this meeting here tonight with a couple of promising rides at disposal that I have found of great interest and will be available on my selections list best of luck to all following and good day to all
Looks very overpriced to me on its handicap debut. For me, this one has run with some ability in every race. I wouldn't take this filly lightly, and at the prices, it's well worth a go.

My bet of the day is Believe the Storm. The horse is the most unexposed in the field and seems to run well on the all-weather surface, on which he won on debut and also came 2nd here at Kempton while giving plenty of weight away to the winner. I am quite surprised you can still get 11/4, and I think it'll shorten before the off. Signs of trainer hitting a bit of form after a quiet spell. NAP

Believe The Storm looks one to note, but I have a preference for this Roger Varian horse who did run well at Leicester last time out and should like the return to all-weather. Won here over seven but also won over a mile.
Sky Safari is 2 wins from 2 on the AW, and after that disastrous run at Royal Ascot (beaten 35L), connections will be glad to get her back to Kempton Park where she has a 100% strike record.

This is a reasonably competitive Class 4, and Believe The Storm (owned by Basher Watts) could well step forward. However, Al Waqidi has some very good form before his long break and has now raced twice, looking much better last time out. If Saffie can race him handy out of stall 2, I think Believe The Storm will struggle to catch him on the short Kempton straight. 6/1 is good value for an each-way bet.

Kalamunda is a tricky horse to follow, but the ability is well and truly there. Back at Kempton, a course and distance winner here, didn't have the clearest of runs last time out at Chelmsford, managed 4th place. First time cheekpieces are kept on for this run. I expect a big run on the cards.

Although he will now never fulfill the potential he showed in his younger days while trained by Charlie Hills, the Gary Moore-trained Cephalus is still a useful performer at this level. His latest win came over today's mile trip at Southwell in February off just a three lb lower mark than the one of 81 he carries today. He has disappointed at Lingfield and Chelmsford since but could go in here where he is a previous C&D winner today.
The yard and jockey are both going well, and this gelding is well handicapped if recapturing his best run form. He is dropped in trip, and a tongue tie is added to try and ignite that improvement.
Has won three of her last seven races, and the 2 lbs increase for her latest win at Chepstow might not be enough to stop her following up here.

One win and two places in three attempts over course and distance bodes well. Drops in trip after racing over the extended seven furlongs at Chester last time out and Elizabeth Gale in the saddle claims a valuable 7 pound allowance for this top weight.
This one's yard is in flying form. The gelding is a four-time course and distance winner. His last win was off 77, and he's now off 66, and looks very good value at 17/2.

Highly promising gelded son of Havana Gold & Midnight Sky ( Dam's sire Desert Prince ) who very impressively completed a 5 timer of back to back wins towards the end of 2024 was last seen at Yarmouth 35 days ago where finishing 6th/7 however that was his seasonal reappearance run after a 124 day break and he is most certainly entitled to strip fitter and be a lot sharper at the finish this time out with that run under his belt and Havana Sky will highly appreciate this switch to a polytrack surface as he is a much better performer on the polytrack surface rather than the turf currently operating on a mark of 67 E A L Dunlop's inmate looks poised to bounce back here and he is only operating 1lb above his last winning mark here however the last time he won he was a 3yo now as a 4yo this individual should have plenty more performances in the locker just waiting to be unleashed and he can be much better than a mark 67 now as a 4yo jockey Hector Crouch takes the ride and can give this a good shot must be considered
Ran to form, beaten 3L off 64 at Chelmsford last run. Good jockey booking, conditions to suit, and running off the same mark as last run. Improvement expected, each way chance.

An intriguing entry having joined Karl Burke's yard and being ridden tonight by a jockey who has won twice from three rides on this horse. Historically, hits form at this time of year, and though absent since last year, connections know how to prepare a horse for a successful reappearance.

This evening Heather Main's Iconic Times returns to Kempton's all-weather, where he got off the mark over this C&D in November. He ran better than the bare result suggested at Sandown last time. With fitness now on his side and back at a track that clearly suits, we could see him go in again.

Three places and a win in the last five runs since changing yard back in February. The win back in May came here in a field of eleven before a decent 3rd last time out at Lingfield. Has another decent draw here to boost things further.

Fiorella Princess is in stall number 8. This 3yo filly by Sands Of Mali has shown her best form on the AW, including a win over this distance, and she now returns to that surface after two below par turf efforts. She has a tongue tie and hood combination for the first time, which may help settle her, as she has raced very freely before. Her only win came on synthetic going, and she holds a 33% win rate and 33% place rate at this trip, along with a 16.67% win rate in this class. Trained by Lemos Souza and ridden by George Wood, she has 6 career runs with a win and 2 placings, giving her a 16.67% win rate and 50% place rate overall. The draw is not ideal, but to me she is on a workable mark. With conditions back in her favour, she is capable of outrunning her odds. Each-way chance if settling better and breaking on time at 33/1

The Tony Carroll 8yo is in fine fettle winning 3 times in the last fortnight and comes here to make it 4. Plenty of weight to carry but Matthew Slater rides again as he has the last 3 times, takes off an important 5lb, and there is no reason to suggest his winning will stop here.
Off a dangerous mark and can certainly be involved in today's race. Definite value in an each-way bet in case the favorite continues to be too good.

Lequinto is the odds-on favorite, having won 3 on the bounce. But the 8-year-old Tony Carroll-trained gelding is rather short in the betting as he's got to carry a double penalty. The Edward Smyth-Osbourne-trained Sarafina Mshairi could be an each-way alternative. The 3-year-old Cable Bay filly ran really well for a long way on her seasonal debut last week, and these conditions should suit her better.
The 4yo is on top of his game, going close in his last three races, the winner from each of those races having won again since. Weighted to run a big race and worth another chance.
Having previously won off much higher marks, Faustus is worth an each-way punt to return to form. If that is the case, the nap can push the hot favorite all the way.
Won nicely at Goodwood last time out and holds the edge over the rest of the field in this one.
Vocal Legend won after a break in April. When third up, he bounced back to take second last time out. What catches my eye is the booking of Colin Keane, which gives the ride an extra tick.
Cairdeas 3 year old chestnut gelding. Slowly coming down the handicap despite running ok in some nice handicaps. This new rating should give him a chance of winning this.

An open-looking handicap where Imperial Trooper makes some appeal at a big-looking 16/1. He has dropped to a good mark and could get his own way out in front. The drop back in trip looks a good move and wasn't beaten far on his last outing at Sandown in a similar race.
A beaten favourite over a mile at Kempton last time out and of interest dropping in trip and trying 7 furlongs for the first time.

Trainer Warren Greatrex reports that Ruff Justice is having her first run back after the injury she sustained during her last run. She will no doubt come on for the run, but if she is up for it today, the 3-year-old Without Parole filly could go close. After all, she has the best speed rating in the field.

Two turf runs for the 4yo this year. Something amiss last time out. He was a good 3rd of 12 during May after coming off a 4 month break and that form looks decent. A 2lb lower mark now, good jockey booking, every chance in this company and too early to write off.
Ran well on debut at Windsor recently and brought out again fairly quickly. A repeat of that run from a stable with a decent record here should see him being a lot nearer today.

The Warren Greatrex-trained, Ed Greatrex-ridden Lope El Fuego ran well on her racecourse debut and will have learnt a lot from that. She should see a big step forward here today and at 11/1 is worth an each-way play.

She finished 4th of 6 in her debut run at Chepstow last month. The expectation is that she will improve and is helped by stable factors like the same class, distance, and similar conditions this time out.
I also like the look of Moo Deng, who made some improvements LTO when 4 of 8 at Chelmsford, which was impressive after her challenging debut run at Newmarket back in May of this year.
The Ed Walker trained Tapioca Pearl has been well found in the market. The 3yo Almanzor filly has just had the 3 runs, is open to improvement and will handle the ground.
Cheekpieces added for the first time. Probably needed as he was green on reappearance on penultimate start and was short of room last time. There should be a better performance in him.

Last time out was beaten at this course, but that was the first good performance this season. I'm happy to back Geo to win today. He has always performed well here and has won last year off a mark of 71 at this track. With this horse coming to form, it looks like the time to back Geo.
Tolerance shaped as if this step up in trip will be very useful. Cheekpieces worked last time out, I think, with Pat Cosgrove taking over. This is what this one needs to break its maiden.

Lightly raced 4yo. He’s not done a lot wrong in his last two starts, no clear passage two runs back and was too far back for a serious challenge last time out. He is down to a handy looking mark now. Just one previous run on quick ground, on his debut last Aug, when going close and posting a high RPR rating.
Showed some potential when 3rd of 6 at Leicester back in May of this year and should offer much more in handicap debut, which is also helped by a drop down in class.

This horse got within a length of a couple of 82-rated horses in his first two runs. This well-bred gelding could be seriously well in here on debut for a stable that is flying with their small stable at the moment. The horse races off just 64 now, and the trainer has given the horse a 3-month break before racing the horse. The booking of Fallon suggests he means business. Looks way overpriced to me at 18/1 (and currently friendless in the early market).
Elly Bay ran well first time out at Leopardstown three weeks ago when a close 3rd of 17 over a mile where main rival Red Autumn finished 7th nearly five lengths behind. Looks the likely winner.

2024 Fred Winter Juvenile Hurdle winner. Classy sort trained by Joseph O'Brien just failed to hold the lead over slightly further at Listowel last time. Beaten less than a length. Amateurs race again but JL Gleason replaces Miss A Connor. Will take some beating and appeals despite being quite strong odds on.

Arch Empire to upset the favorite for mine. I think the key to this race is the distance, and most will struggle with it, whereas Arch Empire is probably best suited to it than most. At the price, I'd usually go with more for a place than a win with such a cramped favorite in a field like this, but I wouldn't be surprised to see him top the favorite off given the lack of depth in this field generally.
Third when last seen over CD at the end of last year behind Taponthego. That one went on to run well when 4th behind Wodhooh at the Cheltenham Festival earlier this year.

Showed a bit in a couple of bumpers before making his hurdling debut at Ballinrobe at the back end of May. Had anything but a hard ride in finishing 4th and looks likely to improve a fair bit on that effort here going up in trip.

Parkside Lad has had two decent runs in better class at the Curragh and at Navan finishing 5th of 21 and 4th of 12 respectively and he should be able to overcome the outside draw around the dogleg at Bellewstown.

Wasn’t beaten far on her first start at Cork in a 5f maiden, doing well to finish as close as she did after having anything but a clear passage during the race. Not in the same form back there next time just two weeks later, but bounced back to form with a close 2nd finish at Hamilton last time. She remains capable of better and can reward each way support.
Showed plenty of pace last time that will suit at this track. Good jockey. Good draw. What's not to like?

Siouxfonic is a 4-year-old son of Sioux Nation ex Velvet Ribbon. He makes his racecourse debut in this 4-year-olds only bumper as a colt. He'll be ridden by Mr. P.W. Mullins for T. Cooper. He wears a tongue tie on this, his debut outing. He may be one for your horse tracker. I make him my Nap of the day.

Ebony King is a 4-year-old gelding sired by Berkshire (8/42 wins in bumpers). He makes his bumper debut for dual-purpose trainer Andrew Slattery. He is out of a dam who was a three-time winner, RPR 122, for Henry DeBromhead, called Une Lavandiere (FR). She was a half-sister to Gibbes Bay, who won on bumper debut. The experienced Mr. A. P. Ryan rides, and he has picked up 15 wins in bumpers (6 of them making debut), and 5/15 wins were for Andrew Slattery. So, Ebony King has to be respected on debut.

The model I run suggests Silly Mongoose can win this one. Silly Mongoose lines up here with an RPR that's the highest of all the runners here. Is not penalized for it in the weights and has Alan O'Sullivan on board relieving a further 7 lbs. Tries the hood for the first time to aid concentration and is one of the few to have run a race before, which experience is helpful at this level. The model has issued a 'moderate' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

JACK SPURS comes from a yard who do well with their runners in the Bumper sphere. This newcomer has a solid enough looking page making him of interest on debut , so as is often the case in races of this nature the market can reveal more.

Junkyard Dog has been in good form so far this year with 1 win as well as finishes of 4th, 5th, and 5th in the only four outings of the year so far. Making hurdles debut here and is being thoroughly respected by the market, installed as favorite to make an immediate winning start.

The model I run suggests Felicity Smoak can win this one. This is a very data-light race, but this young group of horses does have some small weight differentials and trainer form. The trainer has a high RTF% for this one, and coupled with the lighter load to carry around this 2m trip makes the difference. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The Banger Doyle has finished 2nd in his last two chases for which he is much higher rated at 140 than his hurdles mark of 109. He has not been better than 3rd in any of his eleven runs over hurdles but this is a decent chance for his first hurdles win.

FREE FLOW should be ready for a handicap hurdle over the minumum trip and his recent debut in this sphere was likely over a trip too far. He is race-sharp effective on ground as quick as he faces today and the form of his recent maiden hurdle win reads well enough for him handicapping from a mark of 112.

The jockey booked on this one has won 3 of his last 12 rides for the stable, and the horse has slipped to his lowest mark since finishing 3rd of 19 at Punchestown last year. Straight after that, he was sent off as short as 7/2 for this jockey when unseating him early. That was off 105, so he's 2lb lower now, and rather than getting 7/2, we are getting 40/1. So, I think it's fairly easy to make a case for the horse being the value here.

The model I run suggests an upset from Star Official. This result has been driven by Star Official having an RPR that is the second highest in this larger 16-horse race. A mid-ranking official ranking leaves this horse looking reasonably well treated off this mark. Shown glimpses of good form and coupled with the jockey claiming seven lbs off could go close. A total weight being carried near the bottom and looks to come on from the 4th place finish last time out. Trip before that was a win at this distance. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Followed 2nd place finishes in May and June last year with a win at Killarney in July. Not as good in 2 races since, but holds an each-way chance if rediscovering that form from last year.
This one needs to put some mediocre runs behind him, but now sporting a tongue tie for his in form yard, he's worth risking at a huge price.

Willie Mullins saddles three in this race, including Winter Fog, who won this race last year. However, the stable jockey has decided to ride Gaucher. Gaucher is a former course and distance winner. Since that win, he has had five runs, and Paul Townend didn't ride him in any of those. He did win at Naas back in March. The last time Paul Townend rode Gaucher, he won, so I'm taking him to do so again.
Jesse Evans is a bit inconsistent but has been mixing it between flat, hurdles, and chasing. Despite a recent win over hurdles, he is well-weighted in this Grade 3 hurdle.
There are a few with good chances in this race that looks wide open. I am going to go with Winter Fog, who has been so consistently placing and winning, and should go close or win again here.

Won the Fred Winter impressively before disappointing slightly in the G1 Aintree race. Maybe needed more recovery time, and with this being an easier race and having been freshened up, is worth an each-way bet here.
Improved effort last time out and looked like Slevin was starting to get a good tune out of him. Up in class here in a competitive race but a value option to be in the frame.

The model I run suggests Enniskerry can win this one. Enniskerry lines up here with an RPR that is the third highest but goes out carrying a lighter weight load than the potential would suggest. Some good form figures from his last few outings with a first and second place finish, but has been out of action for half a year now. Needs to run well fresh and probably explains the fairly large odds on offer. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Returns after a long layoff. Made stable debut last April and ran only twice last year. Won both starts with new trainer. Despite absence, is a progressive 5-year-old. Danny Mullins on board is a plus.

Sunchart (20/1) rates a value pick for this competitive Grade 3 hurdle. He races over the flat as well as hurdles, and his form figures over hurdles read 432121 (debut run was 4th). His penultimate hurdle run back in October 2024 saw him just touched off by today's hot favorite, Gaucher. A lot can happen over that time period, but he's 5lb better off with that rival today. I think the main danger is the youngster, PUTYOURHANDSTOGETHER (7/1).
Undefeatable went down by half a length on reappearance, and the form from his penultimate run has been boosted with that horse winning at Tipperary. He can go one better in this race.

Worth an interest if staying this far. Then I can see this O'Sullivan runner recouping recent losses. Got outpaced over seven last time out but did run well. Last try at this distance was on heavy going, which was unsuitable.
Eric Lock was 9th of 16 at Fairyhouse three weeks ago. That was over six furlongs. He won a fortnight earlier at Down Royal over the distance, and that performance puts him into the frame.

A seven-race maiden, she looked unlucky two starts ago at Ballinrobe when having anything but a trouble-free run at crucial times in the race. That was in an extended 9f maiden but ran no sort of race back in a handicap over 10f at Fairyhouse last time. Has a bit to prove on the back of that, and minor honors at best looks the likely scenario.

3 y/o James The Second did everything right 2 runs back in Limerick. Took it up at the furlong pole, kicked on and looked home for all money but unfortunately got collared close home. 10lb claimer Terry Casey gave him a great ride but just met one too good. He missed the kick at Down Royal LTO, so we have to put a line through that. A repeat of the Limerick run, albeit with an extra furlong to contend with, would surely see him on the premises. 3lb more to carry wouldn’t put me off. He’s taking on his own age group today after 2 attempts against the older horses..

Not a great race and not one to be getting heavily involved in stake-wise, but I like these sorts of races because they always look like throwing out a big-priced winner. Jess Harrington's Academe came 2nd two races ago in the first handicap run with a pro jockey, but last time out over slightly further, faded when losing the lead in the last furlong. Down in trip today, but I wasn't convinced it didn't get the trip. It looked more like a loss of rhythm after going off too quick. We also have a change of headgear today and I'm hoping Academe can get back on track.

Andrew Slattery's 4-year-old gelding EXCEEDING gets the slight nod ahead of one of today's rivals (I'm sure this will blow up in my face) TAKEACHANCEJIMMY. This son of EXCEED AND EXCEL has made a little progress the past two runs on the turf and in this low-grade affair may have found an opportunity to shed his maiden tag. Trainer has jocked off the apprentice in favour of his more experienced son, who has been ticking along whilst not pulling up any roots the last month (27.78% place strike rate), and his 31.43% place strike rate here the past 5 years certainly shouldn't be overlooked, although his father's 71.43% place strike rate here the past year is very impressive. Running off bottom weight here at current odds of 14/1, I'm happy to side with this potential improver.
Was only caught close home last time out at Gowan, but there was plenty of distance to the third that day. A repeat of that run might be enough to see this one win.
Hasn't done a lot wrong since joining this stable from the UK. Only beaten a length by a gambled-on rival and should feature again.
Eagles Whistle is consistent, ran solidly last time, and now drops to a more suitable trip; capable of handling conditions and has place form. Well weighted to challenge in an open contest.

Going with Roman Harry in this open-looking handicap. Though only recording one victory so far in his career, he has run well in most of his other races, including last time at Limerick. If producing the same level of form here tonight, he could certainly be good enough to be involved in the finish.
This is the trainer's only entry he's got out today as they are stepping it back up to 8f with a 7lbs claiming jockey booking/change. A good value each way bet for the 4 places available.
7-time winner who made a pleasing reappearance when finishing 2nd over this course and distance in April. Holds an each-way chance on that form.

VANGELIS ran a fair race last time out and that was his second start following a break. He has the blinkers added potentially ready now and he does look like a favourably treated four year old given a chance by the assessor. He could be the one who rates a ' dark-horse ' in this handicap.

It was good to see Jack Kennedy return to action on Tuesday after a lengthy spell out injured. If he fails to win on either of his two earlier rides today he looks to have a solid chance of getting a winner aboard this handicap debutant, who has posted some solid efforts in four maiden hurdle races.

FOLLY BEACH is still just a seven year old , so she should be capable odf making an impact switching back into the NH code in handicap hurdles division. Interestingly she has been sharpened up with a couple of runs on the level and with a first-class jockey booked today she could surprise.

The blinkers worked the trick for Kieran Purcell's YOU DONE WELL under Danny Gilligan LTO in Limerick, and it might pay to stay onside with the Kilkenny handler's 4 y/o who could be on the rise. Danny Gilligan retains the ride. Slight jump in class, hopefully the 5lb penalty won’t stop him improving. The extra furlong should help. Loads in with a chances here, so a tentative ew poke from me.

The model I run suggests Way Down South can win this one. This result has been driven by Way Down South having the highest OR of this larger 16 horse race. Looks reasonably well treated in the weights and is certainly not penalized for having a higher RPR. 15s is a big price and is probably based on form. Has won in the last 5 outings but not much shown since. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Won LTO on handicap debut and has been hit with a 12lb rise. It has to be said though, he made that win look very easy and IMO this 5yo can take that rise in his stride. Up slightly in distance should be no problem on the evidence of that last race and I am very happy to take this 25-1 EW.

At current 33/1 odds, I think Eoin Griffin's 8-year-old gelding NAVIGATOR JACK is a tad high as he drops in trip, weight, and class. This son of FAME AND GLORY was running his race 25 days ago at Punchestown and was bang there about 2f out but faded and then slipped. Looking at this charge’s best efforts, 20f is clearly his preferred trip, and he now races off his last winning mark.
It’s also interesting to note that the majority of this lad’s better form has come at sharper tracks, more precisely left-handed, sharp tracks such as Wexford, Bellewstown, Listowel, and here at Tipperary. The conditional jockey is replaced by pro Ricky Doyle, who has a 21.05% place strike rate here over the past five years, while the trainer boasts a very impressive 50% place strike rate at the course over the same period.
A drop back to a favourable trip, back on his last winning mark, and returning to a sharp track - there are simply too many positives for me to ignore, especially at this price. This Charge could represent a touch of value and is certainly worth a second look.
Cabaret Prince is a former winning pointer who has shown up well in three maiden hurdle races before fading late on and his opening mark looks fair for this handicap hurdle.
Got up close to home to beat Jack Turn here over three miles. Plus, up seven pounds for that, but might have still more to offer over this slightly shorter trip.

Co Clare handler Brian McMahon looks to hold a chance here with LOUGHRASK RAINBOW. This 7 y/o came from another parish to finish a close-up 4th at Sligo LTO (25/1-8/1). I thought James Smith gave it a poor ride with too much to do. That was over 2 miles 5, the extra 2 furlongs might bring out a bit more improvement. Handicapper adds 1lb, James Smith retains the ride. It’s competitive, but he’d have a squeak I’d imagine.

Captain Kate had her best result yet when 2nd last time out at Wexford in a three-mile hurdle. Even up a pound, she lurks at the bottom of the handicap off her mark of 73, with Patrick M O'Brien taking off seven pounds to ride at nine stone eight pounds.

Eoin Doyle's 9-year-old gelding RANGER BILLY is certainly a lot better than he showed 26 days ago at Punchestown, where he was pulled up. But this was after a 231-day absence, so I'm a bit more inclined to look past that. This son of WESTERNER drops again in the weights to a very dangerous mark of 91, just 1 lb higher than his last victory last October at Fairyhouse under today's returning jockey Donagh Meyler. This sharp track shouldn't cause too much trouble (should he be fit) with a 45.45% place strike rate when running at similar style tracks. At the current price of 25/1 with 5 places on offer, I'm more than happy to side with this charge who lurks on a very dangerous mark.
Very much an improver and won comfortably last time. Goes up 6 lb here, which with a bit of improvement, has a good chance of following up.
Only Spoofing still has ability, having already won this year and has won before off much higher ratings. Worth chancing each way in case a return to form is imminent.

Lariat won over course and distance in 2022 and has drifted down the handicap to a lowly mark of 43. He more often runs over hurdles and has had a recent 2nd of 18 at Listowel, beaten only half a length, so should be competitive here at the finish against some suspect stayers.
Was slightly fancied to go well in first handicap last time out and did show some better form. Now upped in distance, which might well suit, and might go well off this weight.
Won this race off the same mark last year. Is due a big run to capitalize on sliding handicap mark.

Going to give Ally Cay a chance here today after she returned to the track last month after a very long absence. Ran okay as well, coming 9th/20, and should be sharper today after that run. Big odds at 40-1, and they could just be using these flat races to get her fit for the jump season. But she has won on the flat, and I'm not sure this 9-year-old is nearing retirement just yet.
